<!--

I personally don't use google tts, but this has been tested successfully by @hmmbob (thanks!).

This PR should fix the google TTS functionality. The reason for that is described in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/43258 as well as the analysis of the new API structure.

It also cleans up the code a bit as most of the stuff is done in the library already including message chunking and language checking. I only added the languages again as HA uses it in the Schema and would most likely want to keep it this way. The languages are defined here in the lib:

- https://github.com/pndurette/gTTS/blob/master/gtts/lang.py#L35

pr_comments:
Tested the changes, works for me.

```yaml
tts:
  - platform: google_translate
```
Message is played in English if service is called with just a message ✔️ 
Message is played in Dutch if service is called with message and `language: nl `

```yaml
tts:
  - platform: google_translate
    language: nl
```
Message is played in Dutch if service is called with just a message ✔️ 

Also tested a longer message (the actual weather report, lol) as well. Message is playing completely, but "chunking" is audible. I guess this is due to the type of TTS (Google Translate) and not necessarily a code problem - but I might be wrong there.
Thanks for the test fixes. I was just on it but you were faster.

issue_context.title: Google Translate TTS is no longer working
issue_context.body:

  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases

  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->

Recently there was an update to the google translate platform and the TTS code HA uses will no longer work in the future. (The changes from google are already progressively rolling out, but probably not all countries/regions got them already)

There has been an update of the `gTTS` library that handles this, but apparently HA doesn't use this - probably because it's using the `requests` package instead of the `aiohttp` package. The maintainer of the lib would really like if we could integrate it into HA instead of the `gTTS-token` and is willing do to any changes required in order to make this happen.

Please find all relevant information here: https://github.com/pndurette/gTTS/issues/232

The new Google TTS "API" is very well documented here: https://github.com/Boudewijn26/gTTS-token/blob/master/docs/november-2020-translate-changes.md

It would be great if someone from the core devs could have a look and reply to the issue above directly because the fix implemented in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/42911#issuecomment-724712969 will not work. It's just a retry mechanism, but if the old API is not there anymore it doesn't help.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.117.0
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known):  0.117.0
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Core
- Integration causing this issue: google_translate
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tts/


## Additional information

https://github.com/Boudewijn26/gTTS-token/blob/master/docs/november-2020-translate-changes.md
comments:
> The maintainer of the lib would really like if we could integrate it into HA instead of the `gTTS-token` and is willing do to any changes required in order to make this happen.

Hi! Maintainer of the lib here. Wanted to chime in that `gTTS-token` was originally forked of from `gTTS` (hence the name) by @Boudewijn26 b/c it changed way more often than `gTTS` itself, and it allowed many projects (such as HA) to use it. However with the new changes on the Google Translate side, `gTTS-token` (in its current state) isn't relevant anymore, as the whole scheme changed.

Google itself is providing a [text to speech library](https://github.com/googleapis/python-texttospeech) which is free for 1 million characters/month.
I've switched for my projects already to the google api as it provides a better quality and more options than the google translation api.

@coreGreenberet Good stuff, but I think that the reason why the Google Translate TTS is in Home Assistant is because it allows one to easily setup a TTS capability free of charge - without the need of creating a cloud subscription. Same applies to the [Microsoft Speech integration](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/microsoft/): it'll need one to setup a cloud subscription, and even though both have fairly large free tiers, it _is_ an extra step. With the Google Translate TTS integration none of this applies: "it just works" (well, if it is fixed).

But the Google cloud-text-to-speech could be a nice new integration, if you're up to it?

> But the Google cloud-text-to-speech could be a nice new integration, if you're up to it?

@hmmbob , do you mean [this](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/google_cloud/)?  But agree with you that it requires some extra steps.  While Google Cloud does have better quality, a base free tier Google Translate TTS is great, if fixed.

Yeah, that is what I meant. Never realized it was already in... 🤦‍♂️ 
Free tier until 4 million (standard voice) or 1 million (WaveNet / Neural voices) characters per month, but you do need to setup an account with payment method though. So if one doesn't want to set this all up, the Google Translate TTS is still the easiest way forward indeed.

review_comments: This is now handled inside the lib. Don't need a test.

```suggestion
            _LOGGER.exception("Error during processing of TTS request %s", exc)
            return None, None
```
We should return here, so it does not try to get the value of `mp3_data`
We don't need to pass in `hass` anymore now. 🎉
There is only 1 error type, that's when it raises gTTsError so I removed all other types of tests.
